title: Method-Driven Tests (Structural Coupling)
pattern: A test suite designed to structurally mirror the exact files, classes, and methods of the production codebase (one test method per production method).
why_bad: Structural coupling. It binds tests to the system's internal structural organization [277]. When code is refactored (e.g., splitting a class, extracting methods), the tests are forced to break and be rewritten even if the public behavioral contract remains identical [186, 277].
detection: A 1:1 structural correspondence between the production code layout and the test code layout, particularly using test names derived directly from production method names [241].
counterexample: Behavior-oriented test layouts verifying complete scenarios (using conventions like given-when-then) regardless of how many methods are invoked [75, 242].
fix: Structure tests to focus on verifying **behaviors** and use cases instead of individual methods [186]. Test public contracts and allow internal implementations to shift freely [186, 277].
source:
*   *Clean Architecture*, "Structural Coupling / Fragile Tests" (p. 251-253) [275, 277]
*   *Software Engineering at Google*, "Test Behaviors, Not Methods" (p. 241-246) [186, 241]
